summary:
Space Heritage" is an interactive educational web platform designed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to document and explore humanity's footprints beyond Earth. We developed a comprehensive digital archive that maps out historical spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific instruments left behind on the Moon, Mars, and other celestial bodies.
​The project directly addresses the challenge by transforming complex space mission data into an accessible, engaging, and structured timeline backed by official NASA archives. It highlights the physical legacy of space exploration—distinguishing between operational equipment and historical artifacts. This project is vital because it preserves the collective memory of human space achievements, sparks public curiosity, and serves as an educational bridge connecting space enthusiasts and researchers to humanity’s greatest milestones in the cosmos. (132 words)
details:
• What it does & How it works: "Space Heritage" is an interactive web platform that serves as a digital archive and timeline for human artifacts left beyond Earth. It works by organizing space mission data (such as lunar landers, Mars rovers, and deep-space probes) into a clean, filterable interface. Users can explore destinations (Moon, Mars, etc.), filter equipment types, sort records chronologically, and view detailed modal cards containing historical context, current statuses, and direct links to official NASA science archives.
  • ​Benefits & Intended Impact: The platform bridges the gap between raw scientific data and public accessibility. Its intended impact is to spark public curiosity, inspire the next generation of space explorers, and preserve the historical narrative of space exploration by showcasing humanity's physical footprint across the cosmos.
  • ​Tools, Languages & Software: The project was developed using modern web technologies: HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript for the frontend interface and interactivity, hosted on Vercel for fast deployment and reliable performance. Mission data is integrated and linked directly with official NASA resources and the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA).
  • ​Creativity & Team Considerations: What makes our project creative is its unique perspective: instead of focusing only on active missions, it reframes abandoned and historical spacecraft as "space heritage" or archaeological sites of humanity. The team carefully considered user experience (UI/UX) to ensure the interface is responsive, lightweight, and visually engaging, while maintaining strict factual accuracy by cross-referencing reliable NASA databases.
